_about: OWASP Risk Rating Methodology: every factor is rated 0-9, likelihood and impact are the (weighted) average of their factors, each average becomes LOW (<3) / MEDIUM (<6) / HIGH, and the severity matrix combines the two levels. Curves are [input, rating] points joined by straight lines; inputs past the last point get the last rating.

tracking_load._about: sum over tracker domains of category weight x prevalence modifier (more and more widespread trackers = higher). Weighted 3x so the amount of tracking drives likelihood; the three 'worst single tracker' factors below would otherwise max out on one Google tag

tracker_severity._about: the most invasive tracking category present on the page

tracker_reach._about: highest prevalence among tracking companies present (how much of the web that company can see)

fingerprinting._about: highest Tracker Radar fingerprinting score (0-3) among tracker domains

data_leakage._about: share of leak-limiting headers missing on the main page, weighted

transport_security._about: TLS version of the main page plus a penalty for missing HSTS, capped at 9

cookie_protection._about: average weakness of first-party cookies (a share, so many cookies are not punished for the count alone)

framing_protection._about: rating when neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors is set

category_severity._about: 0-9 rating per Tracker Radar category; a tracker counts as 'tracking' at or above tracking_threshold

tracking_load._about: each tracker domain adds weight (from its category rating 0-9, via this curve) times a prevalence modifier

severity_matrix._about: rows = impact level, columns = likelihood level (OWASP table)

grades._about: severity -> letter grade and its 0-100 band; the number moves inside the band by (likelihood + impact) / 18

owasp_top10._about: OWASP Top 10 (2021) category per finding - change the edition here if your course uses 2025
